threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get confused at the bus stop when the driver doesn’t bother to announce the stops. Proper locals just know when to jump off.
Caught a guy on the 57 chatting up the driver about how he once found a lost pet hamster on a bus. Driver seemed genuinely interested.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a group of kids using old subway tickets as skateboards on the sidewalk—only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find a techno party in a public sauna here. Only in Berlin do you sweat it out in drum and bass during the day and dance at night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they know the exact bus schedule for the 22 Fillmore, even with the delays. Tourists just complain about it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading a crowd in front of the Muni stop on Larkin, harmonica in one hand, coffee in the other. Only in SF do bus delays turn into impromptu concerts.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the heart is really in the small plazas where locals sip vermut and gossip, not in the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the tram stops – overly scanning maps, yet somehow still missed the ‘bon dia’ from locals.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' like it’s a magical portal, not just another overcrowded train. Locals just call it 'the Overground' for the bit that isn't.
Last Friday on the N35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old soul classics. Never knew a late-night ride could feel like a show!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was in Neukölln when I saw four different street musicians serenading each other at Hermannplatz, each in their own world but somehow in sync.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a café that opens at 6 AM, packed with club kids just finished partying and early risers grabbing coffee side by side.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here if they can tell the difference between a BART delay and a MUNI meltdown without checking their phone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a guy serenading commuters on the 19 Polk, while someone else was juggling bottles. Only in the Tenderloin can you witness such bizarre talent mashups.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the park is just for lounging; locals use it for late-night jogs and impromptu dance sessions under the stars.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a new arrival by their struggle with the T-10 card machine; they always look puzzled and miss the 'buy' button.
